rationale: One randomized non-Parkinson depression trial reports lower DASS-21 scores when nigella oil extract is added to sertraline versus sertraline alone (PMID35548175, 18.6 vs 23.4, p<.001, with a one-point arithmetic discrepancy in printed change). A ground-seed premenstrual trial favored a composite mood domain rather than depression severity (PMID41267796), while crushed-seed Bond-Lader mood (PMID24412554) and mixed-product depression trials in hypothyroidism (p=.79) and multiple sclerosis were inconclusive, and a hemodialysis trial has unreported HADS results. Oil preparation, co-treatment, reporting discrepancy, and absence of toasted-seed or Parkinson trials keep the easing lean at minimal_signal. A distinct 2025 rat experiment reports lower forced-swim immobility under oral ethanol seed extract. Group estimates are graph-read and a separate general locomotor control is unavailable. It remains contextual for toasted seed and measured Parkinson depression. The matched 2022 hemodialysis results confirm cold-pressed oil, 20 and 21 analyzed, and no posted arm-level HADS values. The protocol and outcome paper are one cohort.

One controlled mouse experiment (Bian 2019; 10 mice per group across six arms, including a positive-control arm) reports lower 20-minute acetic-acid-evoked writhing counts after oral volatile fractions from dry-fried (toasted) and raw huajiao versus vehicle (18.40 and 21.10 dry-fried, 19.50 and 27.20 raw vs 49.60 vehicle), although full-text methods, fried-versus-raw comparison, and botanical species voucher remain unverified. Local application of isolated hydroxy-alpha-sanshool reduced inflammatory mechanical hypersensitivity without altering heat hypersensitivity in mice (PMID23652591), an uncontrolled nine-woman xerostomia series of mixed Zanthoxylum oil capsules noted oral-discomfort gains without placebo (PMC6392883), and a 40-woman placebo-controlled IBS trial of multi-herb daikenchuto was null for abdominal and rectal pain without isolating Sichuan pepper (PMID26486374). Volatile-fraction rather than whole toasted spice, unverified full-text details, multi-herb clinical nullity, and absence of Parkinson pain data keep the easing signal at minimal_signal. The original Chinese record fixes the high/low raw and fried contrast order while leaving the direct processing comparison, voucher and hot-plate values unverified. The separately registered topical mixture has no posted results.

Cooked brown rice and related feed experiments give a favorable timed-climbing signal in iron-exposed flies. Matched wild-type brown-versus-white comparisons are descriptively favorable and the normal cornmeal comparison differs. Rat evidence and a processed human hydrolysate trial give general motor outcomes without a separate clinical postural-stability result. A bridge to the frozen posture endpoint remains unresolved. EXPRESS reports a rice-protein-powder comparison under matched exercise but its accessible original gives no numerical standing result. A black-rice supplement mobility study and the whole-grain lifestyle pilot do not isolate cooked brown rice. A closer cooked dewaxed-rice study measures cognition.

The oil add-on and oil-coupled ultrasound provide indirect pelvic-pain estimates, while the menopause joint-pain comparison was inconclusive. A recovered cancer-treatment trial reports improved aggregate oral symptoms after topical cold-pressed oil plus Solcoseryl. The pain item was unreported. The frozen Parkinson pain direction remains unresolved. The exact publisher and PDF locators are confirmed. The accessible original abstract reports a pain-domain advantage but no magnitude, verified processing grade or Parkinson comparison. The controlled pelvic-pain adjunct abstract gives overall response counts and qualitative pain-domain direction, without an inspectable pain table or verified pressing. The separate completed cold-pressed bladder study has a secondary combined symptom endpoint and no posted results.
